name: Your Mod
about: What the mod is and what it changes, in plain words. 2000 characters.

files.name: your-mod.zip
files.sha256: the 64 hex characters sha256sum prints for your-mod.zip

_game: The slug of the game this mod is for. GET https://elopros.com/api/workshop lists the games that take mods; GET https://elopros.com/api/workshop/<game> shows the kinds each one takes.
_id: Lowercase letters, digits and '-', up to 48 characters. An id belongs to the first repo that publishes it in a game, so a fork picks its own.
_kind: One of the kinds the game takes, e.g. map, skin, mode.
_files: 1 to 8 files. Each url is a release asset of THIS repo: https://github.com/<you>/<this repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>. size is in bytes. The game checks each file's sha256 after download, so a file whose bytes differ is refused.
_optional: license, preview (a .png or .jpg in this repo) and requires (other mod ids in the same game) may be left out. A LICENSE file in the repo is recorded too.
_next: Upload your files to a GitHub release on a public repo, commit this file at the repo's root as elo-mod.json, then paste the repo at https://elopros.com/mods.html#workshop, or POST https://elopros.com/api/workshop/<game>/publish with {"repo": "https://github.com/you/your-mod"}. For an update, make a new release, change version and the files, commit, and publish again. Keys starting with _ are your own notes and are ignored.
